input.rationale: Receipt 023f240cad604dd7874ba0054537bc81 (exit 0) completes all six comparisons and they hold: twelve node observations across the two caught-up runs converged in 0-20ms, and the added run_3_immediate case - the demotion issued as soon as the bootstrapped node reported Leader, the construction closest to the harness whose setup event twice reported a stale self view - also converged in 0-20ms with every node's LastIndex ending at the configuration index and no index_passed_while_stale case. The baseline events show why that variant is not actually behind: with the leader campaigning only after about ten to twenty seconds, the followers already had the configuration and the no-op (LastIndex 2) by the time the leader was observed, so the immediate and caught-up constructions coincide in practice. The suspicion recorded in this question is therefore refuted across both constructions, and the isolated field in the extended-window harness (near_node_self_voter true while the leader's configuration reports the demotion) stays unexplained but does not touch the VerifyLeader finding: quorumSize and verifyLeader read the leader's own configuration, which is unambiguous and corroborated by both far nodes, and the only peer that could have answered inside that partition is the reachable node, exactly as the pre-window control that disconnects it shows. I am recording this as the question's current account and leaving that field documented rather than chased further, because no construction I can build reproduces it while every sampled construction shows the entry arriving immediately.

interpretations.rationale: Predicates: every node converges within ten seconds, and no node's view is old while its own log already holds the configuration entry. All six hold, over twelve node observations in this receipt and the same measurements in the previous one, including the immediate-demotion case (near: converged 20ms, last_index_end 3, stale samples only at LastIndex 2 while the configuration index is 3). The source path is unchanged from the earlier account: a peer's own view is the atomic copy written by setLatestConfiguration from processConfigurationLogEntry while appending new entries, or from installSnapshot, so a lag would require the entry not to arrive; no sample shows a node whose log had the entry while its view was still old, and no sample shows a node lagging at all. The question's suspicion is therefore defeated for the constructions tested: a committed voter-to-non-voter transition is reflected by every peer within about one sample interval. The one observation that motivated the question - near_node_self_voter true in the setup events of the two extended-window executions - is retained as an unexplained artefact of that harness's field: it is not reproduced by any construction with per-node sampling, and it cannot explain the VerifyLeader result either way, because that result is decided by the leader's own configuration (voters 3, nonvoters 1, quorum 2) and by the acknowledgements the leader can obtain, with the far voters unreachable.
limitations: Healthy, unloaded, fully connected in-memory cluster in one process; no contention, snapshot install, restart or partition was combined with the transition, so lags under those conditions remain untested rather than excluded.

Seven runs of the discriminating family across both receipts (three plus four), each sampling every 20ms for ten seconds; a rarer stall would need many more repetitions to bound, and a sub-20ms lag is invisible to this sampling.

The immediate-demotion variant turned out not to differ materially because the bootstrapped leader campaigns only after ten to twenty seconds, by which time the followers are already caught up; a construction where the transition truly precedes the followers' adoption was not achieved.
The configuration index used for the consistency check is the leader's LastIndex after the change returns, not an inspection of each follower's log store.
interpretations.joint_history: Both receipts run the same fixed experiment family from identical inputs (cluster construction, per-node timing, DemoteVoter call, 20ms sampling and measured fields); the newer one adds the immediate-demotion case and the waited_baseline field, so the indices for the caught-up runs carry the same measurements in both.

interpretations.rationale: Declared comparisons: comparison 0 predicted the anomaly (success while only a non-voter is reachable) and comparison 1 and 2 predicted that nothing else produces it; all three are complete and hold over every applicable observation (treatment indices 2, 6, 9; control indices 12 and 15), and the controls differ from the treatment in exactly one property each (suffrage of the reachable node; reachability of that same non-voter). The defect claim is separate from those predicate results: the leader's client-visible confirmation that it may still be treated as leader is satisfied by an acknowledgement from a peer that the target itself defines as not considered for elections or commitment (configuration.go:16-18), while the quorum it is compared against counts voters only (raft.go:1086-1093) and the vote attribution is unfiltered (future.go:274-293 via replication.go:100-111). Under the documented purpose of the call (api.go:880-882) a client that gates reads on VerifyLeader can therefore be told it is safe to read a leader that has lost every voter except itself, until its own lease expires; the first receipt's index 3 shows the majority side committing a write (index 5) that never reached that leader's FSM (applied index 3, write absent). The remaining uncertainty is the length of that window, recorded as the open gap.

counterevidence: Index 3 of 68e243c33c644a32bc7ec9b29f076623: in the only attempt where the voter majority elected a new leader and committed 'assurance-stale-write' (index 5, present in the new leader's FSM, absent from the partitioned leader's, which was at applied index 3), the partitioned leader had already become Follower at the 3386ms sample, so this receipt does not witness a successful confirmation issued after the majority had a competing leader.

Indices 2, 6 and 9 of 68e243c33c644a32bc7ec9b29f076623 and 2, 5, 8 of df528a8a25a04cbd9fb1cc12319f3467 report other_leader_before_result false: no competing leader existed at the instant of the false confirmation, so the immediate harm shown here is a broken confirmation guarantee, not yet an observed stale read served under a competing leader.
limitations: In-memory transports and stores inside one process; no TCP or cross-host partition was exercised, and the partition is imposed by removing transport routes rather than by a real network failure.

The second vote that completes the quorum is attributed to the reachable non-voter by construction (the two controls change only suffrage and reachability); the internal verifyFuture.votes counter was not instrumented.

Only DemoteVoter was exercised as the voter-to-non-voter transition; AddNonvoter and the deprecated Staging suffrage follow the same Suffrage != Voter path in startStopReplication and notifyAll but were not executed.

Two of the three successor treatment attempts saw no far-side leader within the harness's 4s post-confirmation window, so the timing of the majority-side election relative to the leader's lease is only partially characterized.
The 20s result deadline in the harness is not the observation itself: controls report their error when the pending verify future is answered at step-down, which the receipt shows at ~1.98s.
interpretations.joint_history: Both receipts execute one fixed harness (assurance_generated_test.go) from fixed inputs in a clean copy; they differ only in the comparison applicability declarations submitted with the successor, not in initialization, topology, partition, timings or emitted event fields, so the same scenario indices carry the same meaning in both. The older receipt is retained because it is a second, independent execution of the treatment and controls; its per-comparison outcomes were reported incomplete only because each admission alias reached the setup events of its own case.

interpretations.rationale: Declared comparisons and their meaning, kept separate from the defect judgment. Comparison 0 (anomaly prediction: success with only the demoted non-voter reachable) holds on index 2. Comparison 1 (anomaly prediction for the extension, antecedent new_leader_exists true) holds on index 3: the same confirmation is answered with nil at 5509ms while a competing node holds leadership and while the answering leader is still Leader with a 20s lease. Comparison 2 (antecedent new_leader_fsm_has_write true, applicability old_leader_is_leader true) holds on index 4: the payload committed by the competing leader at index 5 is absent from the old leader's FSM, whose applied index is 3 — so a client that follows the documented pattern (confirm, then read) reads state that omits a committed write. Comparison 3 (control) holds on index 7: the identical construction and per-node timing without the demotion yields no competitor and no success, ending in leadership loss at 20003ms. Defect claim: the confirmation is computed against a voter-only quorum (raft.go:1086-1093) but credited by an unfiltered vote path (raft.go:965-987 registering every followerReplication; replication.go:100-111 notifying each; future.go:274-293 counting without suffrage), while the target's own definition states non-voters are not considered for elections or commitment (configuration.go:16-18); therefore a client can be told it is safe to treat a leader that has lost every other voter as leader for the whole configured lease interval, even after a different node holds leadership and has committed writes the old leader never received. The controls in the two earlier receipts (indices 12 and 15 of 68e243c33c644a32bc7ec9b29f076623, indices 11 and 14 of df528a8a25a04cbd9fb1cc12319f3467) already excluded reachability and kept the same reachable node as a voter, so the enabling property remains the unfiltered vote attribution.

answers.101498ecfbb945e0b48676dd9e9f4172-gap-0: Yes, and the bound is the leader's own lease rather than the election interval. In the extended-window execution the partitioned leader answered VerifyLeader successfully at 0ms and again at 5509ms (index 2 and 3), while the voter majority had already elected its own leader and committed a write at index 5 (index 4); the old leader remained Leader at applied index 3 with that write absent from its FSM. The lease path that eventually ends this state is checkLeaderLease, which counts only voters whose last contact is within LeaderLeaseTimeout (raft.go:1036-1060), so the window lasts as long as the configured lease; ValidateConfig only requires LeaderLeaseTimeout <= HeartbeatTimeout (config.go:366-371), so the 20s used here is a legal configuration and the exposure is bounded by that configured value, not by the followers' 3s election time.

in a 4-node cluster with voters {leader, far1, far2} plus one reachable Nonvoter, VerifyLeader returns nil within the same millisecond as the partition, while the same call with that node still a voter, or with it unreachable, returns leadership lost about one LeaderLeaseTimeout later

counterevidence: Index 0: the demoted near node's own configuration still reported itself as a voter when the setup event was emitted, while the leader's configuration and both far nodes reported the demotion. Had the near node still held a vote in the committed configuration, the leader's quorum would have been 3 rather than 2 and the observed success would need another explanation. The recorded quorum is the one the leader reads (quorumSize and verifyLeader use r.configurations.latest), it is corroborated by both far nodes, and the pre-existing fixed experiment derived the same quorum through the cluster helper, so the treatment remains a 2-of-3 quorum; the near node's stale self-view is a separate sourced observation, not an explanation of this result.
limitations: One treatment execution of the extended window (plus its control); the pre-window treatment was executed three times per receipt in the two earlier receipts, but the superseded-leader coincidence was observed once.

Timing: the 20s leader lease is legal (<= HeartbeatTimeout) and only makes an existing window observable; the claim is about the mechanism and the bound, not about this particular value. Deployments with shorter leases see a correspondingly shorter window and the same false confirmation.
In-memory transports in one process; partitions are imposed by removing transport routes rather than by a real network failure, and there is no post-partition healing sample of the old leader's FSM.
The stale read is inferred from the FSM/commit samples and the confirmation result; the harness does not itself perform a client read.

The second VerifyLeader call happens after the harness has observed the competing node in Leader state, but the harness does not prove that the competing leader had already committed anything at the moment of that call; the write was applied immediately afterwards (index 4, same 5509ms).
Only the DemoteVoter transition was exercised; AddNonvoter and the deprecated Staging suffrage take the same Suffrage != Voter path but were not run.

Only the DemoteVoter transition was exercised; AddNonvoter and the deprecated Staging suffrage take the same Suffrage != Voter path but were not run.
interpretations.joint_history: Both receipts belong to the same fixed experiment f86170361cdb4c0fb5317d016675dd6b-experiment and execute its retained harness from fixed inputs in a clean copy; the second is the requested repeat, so indices 2, 3, 4 and 7 carry the same measurements in both (nil after the partition, nil while superseded, the competitor's write absent from the old leader's FSM, and the control losing leadership at the lease).

interpretations.rationale: Predicates: every node converges within ten seconds, and no node's view is old while its own log already holds the configuration entry. All six hold, over twelve node observations in this receipt and the same measurements in the previous one, including the immediate-demotion case (near: converged 20ms, last_index_end 3, stale samples only at LastIndex 2 while the configuration index is 3). The source path is unchanged from the earlier account: a peer's own view is the atomic copy written by setLatestConfiguration from processConfigurationLogEntry while appending new entries, or from installSnapshot, so a lag would require the entry not to arrive; no sample shows a node whose log had the entry while its view was still old, and no sample shows a node lagging at all. The question's suspicion is therefore defeated for the constructions tested: a committed voter-to-non-voter transition is reflected by every peer within about one sample interval. The one observation that motivated the question - near_node_self_voter true in the setup events of the two extended-window executions - is retained as an unexplained artefact of that harness's field: it is not reproduced by any construction with per-node sampling, and it cannot explain the VerifyLeader result either way, because that result is decided by the leader's own configuration (voters 3, nonvoters 1, quorum 2) and by the acknowledgements the leader can obtain, with the far voters unreachable.
limitations: Healthy, unloaded, fully connected in-memory cluster in one process; no contention, snapshot install, restart or partition was combined with the transition, so lags under those conditions remain untested rather than excluded.

Seven runs of the discriminating family across both receipts (three plus four), each sampling every 20ms for ten seconds; a rarer stall would need many more repetitions to bound, and a sub-20ms lag is invisible to this sampling.

The immediate-demotion variant turned out not to differ materially because the bootstrapped leader campaigns only after ten to twenty seconds, by which time the followers are already caught up; a construction where the transition truly precedes the followers' adoption was not achieved.
The configuration index used for the consistency check is the leader's LastIndex after the change returns, not an inspection of each follower's log store.
interpretations.joint_history: Both receipts run the same fixed experiment family from identical inputs (cluster construction, per-node timing, DemoteVoter call, 20ms sampling and measured fields); the newer one adds the immediate-demotion case and the waited_baseline field, so the indices for the caught-up runs carry the same measurements in both.
